transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I came in because I keep hearing these voices, clear like somebody’s standing right there in my little studio. It’ll be quiet, nobody there, and I’ll hear my name, or them saying my work is being judged. And I try to ignore it, you know, like maybe it’s the neighbors or the TV, but I don’t even have anything on sometimes. My place is small, so you can tell when someone’s there… and nobody is.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or that someone is trying to communicate with you in ways others don’t understand?

Yeah… not like somebody has a remote control in my head exactly, but I did get it in my head that people were… watching what I was doing. The other home-care agency, and some people from the library too, like they were looking at my paintings and even my client papers, trying to steal some chance that was supposed to be mine.

And I know people told me, “That doesn’t make sense,” but… see, the library people know everybody, they see what you check out, and I used to go there to look at art books sometimes. Anyway, I just knew they were doing it. I could feel it, like they were putting things together behind my back.
Have you ever felt that thoughts were being placed in your mind that aren't your own, or that events or actions around you were specifically directed at you?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in my head, like… I can’t say it that way exactly. But I did feel like things around me were about me, yes. Like that other home-care agency, and some people at the library, they were watching what I was doing—my paintings, my client papers, all of it.

I used to go to the library for art books, and you know how people there see what you’re checking out, who you talk to… it all connects. Folks told me, “That doesn’t make sense,” but I still knew they were trying to take some chance that was supposed to be mine. I could feel it.
Have you ever felt that things people do around you—like their actions or conversations—are secretly about you or meant to send you a message?

Yes… yes, that’s kind of what I mean. Like I got it in my head that the other home-care agency, and some of those people from the library, were watching what I was doing. My paintings, even my client papers… like they were trying to take some chance that was supposed to be mine.

And people told me, “That doesn’t make any sense,” but they don’t know how people talk, you know? At the library everybody sees things, who comes in, what books you look at… I used to look at art books there, and then it just felt like it all connected. I knew they were doing it, even if nobody else believed me.
Have you ever felt that things happening around you—like things on TV, radio, or even random events—were specifically meant to send you a message or were directed at you personally?

I don’t know if it was like the TV or radio talking straight to me… I don’t really watch the same shows every day, and sometimes the commercials all sound the same anyway. But I did feel like things around me were aimed at me, yes.

Like I said, that other home-care agency, and some people at the library, I got it in my head they were watching what I was doing—my paintings, my client papers, all that. I used to go to the library for art books, and you know, people notice what you’re interested in. And then I felt like they were putting it together, like trying to steal a chance that was supposed to be mine.

People kept saying it didn’t make sense, but… I still knew. I could just tell they were doing it.
Have you ever felt that your actions were being controlled by an outside force, or that thoughts were being put into your mind that didn’t belong to you?

I don’t think controlled, no… not like somebody had a remote on me or anything. And thoughts being put in my head, I don’t know. I get thoughts, same as anybody, and sometimes I think too much, especially when I’m tired or when people keep asking me things and I’m trying to explain it right.

Like with work, you know, when you’re going from house to house and everybody wants something different, it gets in your head. But I can’t say somebody else was putting thoughts in there. I don’t know what that would even feel like, exactly.

Have you ever had any unusual beliefs about yourself that others might not understand, such as thinking you have special powers, a special mission, or are someone important that others don’t recognize?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it special powers, not like that. But I did feel like I had something important that people weren’t seeing yet.

With my artwork, I really believed it was going to get discovered any day, like somebody was going to come across it and say, “This is the one.” I’d be working on pieces and thinking, this is bigger than just me doing paintings at home, you know? And then with the care work… I had this idea that I was supposed to put it together, like a whole care-and-art program. Not just activities, but something doctors and agencies would come learn from me about.

Because I know what it’s like in people’s homes, and I know how art can calm people down or make them remember things, and—well, I used to keep scraps and notes and all kinds of things, and my kitchen table would get covered, then I’d have to move it because I needed to eat. But yes, I really thought it was going to happen, like I was meant to do it and people just didn’t understand yet.

Have you ever felt that other people were talking about you, following you, or trying to harm you in ways beyond what you’ve already described—like in other parts of your life or in different situations?

Mostly it was that same kind of thing, with the agency and the library people. I can’t say somebody was following me everywhere, like in a movie or something, but I felt watched. Like they were noticing my paintings, and even my client papers, and putting things together behind my back.

And see, that’s what people don’t understand, because when you’re a care aide you carry things around, notes and schedules and folders, and sometimes you stop at the library or the store, and people look. They act like they’re not looking, but they look. I used to get art books there too, and then I’d think, well, now they know what I’m working on.

So yes, I thought they were talking about me and trying to take an opportunity that was meant for me. People told me it didn’t make sense, but I still felt like I knew it was happening.
Have you ever had beliefs that something was happening or being done to you that others said wasn’t true, even though you were completely sure it was?

Yes… that happened. I got it in my head that the other home-care agency, and some people at the library, were watching what I was doing. My paintings, and even my client papers, like they were looking at them and putting pieces together.

And I know people said, “That doesn’t make sense, why would they do that,” but at the time I was sure. I mean, when you’re carrying folders around and you stop at the library, and people know you come in for art books, and then they look at you a certain way… it felt like they were trying to take a chance that was supposed to be mine.

People kept telling me I was wrong, but I still felt like I knew.
Are there times when you feel completely certain about something happening to you or being planned against you, even when others say there's no evidence it's true?

Yes… that’s what I mean. I got really certain that the other home-care agency, and some people from the library, were watching what I was doing.

It started with my paintings, but then it felt like they were noticing my client papers too, like they were putting things together and trying to take some chance that was supposed to be mine. And I know people told me, “That doesn’t make sense,” and I’d try to hear that, but I still felt like… no, I know what I’m seeing.

The library thing bothered me because I used to go there for art books, and you know, people see what you check out, they see what you carry. I’d have folders and scraps and notes, and then somebody looks at you a certain way and it just— it felt planned. Like they knew. Even if nobody else believed me.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being taken out of your head, put into your head, or that you were broadcasting your thoughts to others without meaning to?

I don’t know about thoughts being taken out like that… I mean, not exactly. What I keep coming back to is more that people were watching what I was doing.

Like the other home-care agency, and some people at the library — I got it in my head they were looking at my paintings and even my client papers, trying to figure something out and take a chance that was meant for me. And people told me, “That makes no sense,” but at the time I still knew they were doing it.

The library, you know, people see what you carry, what books you’re looking at… so it felt like they knew things. Not so much my thoughts flying out, more like they were watching and putting it together.
Have you ever seen things that others don’t see, or experienced sensations on your body that you couldn’t explain?

I don’t know about seeing things, not like… shapes or people standing there. But I do hear voices. That’s really why I came in, because it’s gotten so clear, like somebody is right there in my little studio with me.

They’ll say my name, and then it’s like they’re saying my work is being judged. My paintings, I mean. And the house will be quiet — nobody there, no TV or anything — and I still hear it.

Sometimes I try to tell myself it’s just the neighbors or something, because sound carries funny, you know, especially when you’re working and you’re tired… but it sounds right there, like a person standing close by.
Have you ever felt that random events, like something you saw on TV or something that happened on the street, were directly related to you or sending you a special message?

Yeah… I mean, not so much TV, I don’t watch a whole lot besides whatever’s on when I’m cleaning up or eating. But out in places, like the library, little things started feeling like they were about me.

Like if somebody looked at my folder, or if they were near the art books after I’d been there, I’d think, okay, they know. They’re watching the paintings. And then with the home-care agency too, it felt connected, like they were looking at my client papers and putting things together to steal some chance that was supposed to be mine.

People kept saying, “That doesn’t make sense,” but at the time I couldn’t let it go. I felt sure. Even the way people moved around or looked over — it felt like it meant something about me.
Have you ever felt that your artwork or your ideas were so important that they would attract special attention from people who wanted to use them for themselves?

Yeah… that’s kind of what I mean. I don’t know if “important” is the word, but I got it in my head that my paintings were being watched, like people could see there was something there.

And it wasn’t just the paintings, it was my client papers too, from the home-care work. That other agency, and then some people at the library — because I go there, I look at art books, I carry my folders around — it felt like they were putting things together. Like they were trying to take some chance that was supposed to be mine.

People told me, “That doesn’t make sense,” and I know how it sounds when I say it out loud. But at the time I still knew they were doing it. I couldn’t shake it.
Have you ever felt that things people do around you — like their gestures, actions, or conversations — are directly related to you, even if they don’t involve you directly?

Yeah… yes, I did. Like if people were talking low or moving papers around, I’d feel like it had to do with me, even if nobody said my name.

It was mostly with the other home-care agency and then some people at the library. I’d be there with my folders, you know, and I’d see somebody looking near the art books or handling papers, and my mind would go straight to, they’re watching my paintings, they’re looking at my client papers. Like they were trying to steal some opportunity that was meant for me.

And I know people told me, “That doesn’t make sense,” but… at the time, I still felt like I knew. I couldn’t just drop it.
Have you ever experienced any other symptoms such as seeing things that aren’t there, feeling sensations on your body with no explanation, or having trouble organizing your thoughts or speech?

Yeah… the voices, mostly. That’s actually why I came in, because I keep hearing them like they’re right there in my little studio, clear as somebody standing next to me.

They’ll say my name, and then it’s about my work being judged, like the paintings or what I’m doing isn’t just mine anymore. And I’ll stop and look around, because the house is quiet, nobody’s there. Sometimes I think maybe it’s the pipes or somebody outside, but it’s too clear for that.

I don’t know about seeing things… it’s more the hearing. And then I get all turned around trying to explain it, because I’ll be thinking about the studio and the canvases and how I should’ve cleaned up better, and then the voice happens again. But yes, I hear it.
Have you ever felt that things like objects, events, or even inanimate things — like how a light flickers or how a car drives by — were sending you a message or had a special meaning just for you?

I don’t know about a light flickering exactly… I mean, sometimes I’d notice things and my mind would go somewhere with it, but the big thing was more people and papers.

Like that other home-care agency, and then some people at the library — because I’d be there with my art books and my folders, and I had my client papers too, which I probably shouldn’t have been carrying around so much, but I was always trying to keep things straight. And I started feeling like they were watching my paintings and looking at my papers, like they knew there was some chance coming for me and they were trying to take it.

People would say, “Why would they do that?” or “That doesn’t make sense,” and I’d hear them, but I still knew it. It felt like it was meant for me and they were moving around it, trying to get it first.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being inserted into your mind, taken out of your mind, or that you were broadcasting your thoughts to others without intending to?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in or taken out like that… not exactly. It was more like I got something in my head and I couldn’t shake it.

Like with that other home-care agency, and then the people at the library — I’d be trying to keep my folders together, my paintings, my client papers, and I’d start thinking they were watching all of it. Like they knew there was a chance meant for me, something with my work maybe, and they were trying to get to it first.

And people would tell me, “That doesn’t make sense,” but it didn’t matter. I still felt like I knew they were doing it.
Have you ever felt that your artwork or your ideas were so special or important that they deserved recognition or attention from others that they weren’t getting?

Yes… I did feel that way. I really thought my paintings were going to be discovered any day, like somebody was going to finally see what I was doing and understand it was important.

And it wasn’t just the art by itself. I had this whole idea in my head about combining care work with art, because I’ve done personal care and I know how people get overlooked, you know? I thought I was supposed to build this whole care-and-art program, and doctors and agencies would come learn from me. Like I had figured out something they hadn’t.

I know that might sound big, but at the time it felt true. Like I was waiting for everyone else to catch up.
